stanzas.sanskrit:
सैरन्ध्र्यास्तदनु चिरं स्मरातुराया
यातोऽभूः सुललितमुद्धवेन सार्धम् ।
आवासं त्वदुपगमोत्सवं सदैव
ध्यायन्त्याः प्रतिदिनवाससज्जिकायाः ॥ ७७-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna went well adorned with Uddhava to the house of Sairandhri who had given sandal paste and was long stricken with love for Krishna. She dressed herself well with costumes and jewellery, decorated her house well and waited for Krishna's arrival.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sairandhryāstadanu ciraṃ smarāturāyā
yāto’bhūḥ sulalitamuddhavena sārdham |
āvāsaṃ tvadupagamotsavaṃ sadaiva
dhyāyantyāḥ pratidinavāsasajjikāyāḥ || 77-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
उपगते त्वयि पूर्णमनोरथां
प्रमदसम्भ्रमकम्प्रपयोधराम् ।
विविधमाननमादधतीं मुदा
रहसि तां रमयाञ्चकृषे सुखम् ॥ ७७-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: At Krishna’s arrival, all her wishes got fulfilled and she welcomed Krishna and happily served HIM various offerings.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
upagate tvayi pūrṇamanorathāṃ
pramadasambhramakamprapayodharām |
vividhamānanamādadhatīṃ mudā
rahasi tāṃ ramayāñcakṛṣe sukham || 77-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
पृष्टा वरं पुनरसाववृणोद्वराकी
भूयस्त्वया सुरतमेव निशान्तरेषु ।
सायुज्यमस्त्विति वदेद्बुध एव कामं
सामीप्यमस्त्वनिशमित्यपि नाब्रवीत् किम् ॥ ७७-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna wanted to grant a boon for her hospitality. Instead of asking for devotion to Krishna throughout her life or asking for HIS presence with her always, this ignorant woman asked HIS presence with her for few nights. Bhattathiri wonders at her ignorance of not asking "saamipyam" (being close with Bhagwan) or "saaujyam" (being one with Bhagwan) from Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pṛṣṭā varaṃ punarasāvavṛṇodvarākī
bhūyastvayā suratameva niśāntareṣu |
sāyujyamastviti vadedbudha eva kāmaṃ
sāmīpyamastvaniśamityapi nābravīt kim || 77-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततो भवान् देव निशासु कासुचि-
-न्मृगीदृशं तां निभृतं विनोदयन् ।
अदादुपश्लोक इति श्रुतं सुतं
स नारदात् सात्त्वततन्त्रविद्बभौ ॥ ७७-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna granted her boon and made her happy the following few nights, as a result a son Upashloka was born to them. He learnt paancharathraagamam from Sage Narada.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tato bhavān deva niśāsu kāsuci-
-nmṛgīdṛśaṃ tāṃ nibhṛtaṃ vinodayan |
adādupaśloka iti śrutaṃ sutaṃ
sa nāradāt sāttvatatantravidbabhau || 77-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अक्रूरमन्दिरमितोऽथ बलोद्धवाभ्या-
-मभ्यर्चितो बहु नुतो मुदितेन तेन ।
एनं विसृज्य विपिनागतपाण्डवेय-
-वृत्तं विवेदिथ तथा धृतराष्ट्रचेष्टाम् ॥ ७७-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna went with Balaraama and Uddhava to Akrurar’s house. Akrura received Krishna with high honours. Krishna sent Akrurar to gather the news of the Pandavaas who had returned from the forest and also news about Dhritaraashtra's doings.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
akrūramandiramito’tha baloddhavābhyā-
-mabhyarcito bahu nuto muditena tena |
enaṃ visṛjya vipināgatapāṇḍaveya-
-vṛttaṃ viveditha tathā dhṛtarāṣṭraceṣṭām || 77-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
विघाताज्जामातुः परमसुहृदो भोजनृपते-
-र्जरासन्धे रुन्धत्यनवधिरुषान्धेऽथ मथुराम् ।
रथाद्यैर्द्योर्लब्धैः कतिपयबलस्त्वं बलयुत-
-स्त्रयोविंशत्यक्षौहिणि तदुपनीतं समहृथाः ॥ ७७-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Jaraasandhan, father in law of Kamsan, was very angry with Kamsa vadham and attacked Mathura. Krishna along with Balaraama, and a few soldiers & chariot called from devaloka destroyed his army of 23 Akshauhini brought by him.
(1 Akshouhini - 21,870 chariots, elephants, 65,610 cavalry and 1,09,350 infantry).
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vighātājjāmātuḥ paramasuhṛdo bhojanṛpate-
-rjarāsandhe rundhatyanavadhiruṣāndhe’tha mathurām |
rathādyairdyorlabdhaiḥ katipayabalastvaṃ balayuta-
-strayoviṃśatyakṣauhiṇi tadupanītaṃ samahṛthāḥ || 77-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
बद्धं बलादथ बलेन बलोत्तरं त्वं
भूयो बलोद्यमरसेन मुमोचिथैनम् ।
निश्शेषदिग्जयसमाहृतविश्वसैन्यात्
कोऽन्यस्ततो हि बलपौरुषवांस्तदानीम् ॥ ७७-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Balarama somehow forcefully tied Jarasandhan who was strongest king in the world at that time, who captured territories in all directions around. To make him come for more fights, Krishna freed him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
baddhaṃ balādatha balena balottaraṃ tvaṃ
bhūyo balodyamarasena mumocithainam |
niśśeṣadigjayasamāhṛtaviśvasainyāt
ko’nyastato hi balapauruṣavāṃstadānīm || 77-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भग्नः स लग्नहृदयोऽपि नृपैः प्रणुन्नो
युद्धं त्वया व्यधित षोडशकृत्व एवम् ।
अक्षौहिणीः शिव शिवास्य जघन्थ विष्णो
सम्भूय सैकनवतित्रिशतं तदानीम् ॥ ७७-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Jarasandhan attacked Krishna 16 times and every time he was defeated. Bhagwan wondrously destroyed all the 391 of his Akshouhini armies altogether.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhagnaḥ sa lagnahṛdayo’pi nṛpaiḥ praṇunno
yuddhaṃ tvayā vyadhita ṣoḍaśakṛtva evam |
akṣauhiṇīḥ śiva śivāsya jaghantha viṣṇo
sambhūya saikanavatitriśataṃ tadānīm || 77-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अष्टादशेऽस्य समरे समुपेयुषि त्वं
दृष्ट्वा पुरोऽथ यवनं यवनत्रिकोट्या ।
त्वष्ट्रा विधाप्य पुरमाशु पयोधिमध्ये
तत्राऽथ योगबलतः स्वजनाननैषीः ॥ ७७-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: When Jarasandhan came for the 18th time, Krishna took help of devaloka architect Vishwakarma and built a palace in Dwaraka amidst the sea and deported all his people to Dwaraka through his yogic powers.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
aṣṭādaśe’sya samare samupeyuṣi tvaṃ
dṛṣṭvā puro’tha yavanaṃ yavanatrikoṭyā |
tvaṣṭrā vidhāpya puramāśu payodhimadhye
tatrā’tha yogabalataḥ svajanānanaiṣīḥ || 77-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
पद्भ्यां त्वं पद्ममाली चकित इव पुरान्निर्गतो धावमानो
म्लेच्छेशेनानुयातो वधसुकृतविहीनेन शैले न्यलैषीः ।
सुप्तेनाङ्घ्र्याहतेन द्रुतमथ मुचुकुन्देन भस्मीकृतेऽस्मिन्
भूपायास्मै गुहान्ते सुललितवपुषा तस्थिषे भक्तिभाजे ॥ ७७-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna then ran away acting in fright. Kaalayavana, friend of Jarasandha chased and Krishna purposefully ran into a cave as Krishna wanted to avoid killing him. Kaalayavana stepped on Muchukunda who was sleeping inside the cave. He was instantly burnt to ashes by the angry look of the awakened king. Pleased with Muchukunda, Krishna showed his Bhagavath Swaroopam to him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
padbhyāṃ tvaṃ padmamālī cakita iva purānnirgato dhāvamāno
mleccheśenānuyāto vadhasukṛtavihīnena śaile nyalaiṣīḥ |
suptenāṅghryāhatena drutamatha mucukundena bhasmīkṛte’smin
bhūpāyāsmai guhānte sulalitavapuṣā tasthiṣe bhaktibhāje || 77-10 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ऐक्ष्वाकोऽहं विरक्तोऽस्म्यखिलनृपसुखे त्वत्प्रसादैककाङ्क्षी
हा देवेति स्तुवन्तं वरविततिषु तं निस्पृहं वीक्ष्य हृष्यन् ।
मुक्तेस्तुल्यां च भक्तिं धुतसकलमलं मोक्षमप्याशु दत्त्वा
कार्यं हिंसाविशुद्ध्यै तप इति च तदा प्रात्थ लोकप्रतीत्यै ॥ ७७-११ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna wanted to grant a boon, but Muchukunda who is a great devotee of Krishna requested only HIS blessings. Moved with his answer, Krishna granted deep devotion which will give him moksham. Krishna told him to do penance to purify the deeds for the pain caused to people during his rule.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
aikṣvāko’haṃ virakto’smyakhilanṛpasukhe tvatprasādaikakāṅkṣī
hā deveti stuvantaṃ varavitatiṣu taṃ nispṛhaṃ vīkṣya hṛṣyan |
muktestulyāṃ ca bhaktiṃ dhutasakalamalaṃ mokṣamapyāśu dattvā
kāryaṃ hiṃsāviśuddhyai tapa iti ca tadā prāttha lokapratītyai || 77-11 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तदनु मथुरां गत्वा हत्वा चमूं यवनाहृतां
मगधपतिना मार्गे सैन्यैः पुरेव निवारितः ।
चरमविजयं दर्पायास्मै प्रदाय पलायितो
जलधिनगरीं यातो वातालयेश्वर पाहि माम् ॥ ७७-१२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Krishna returned to Mathura after Kaalayavana vadham and killed his armies. Jarasandha once again obstructed Krishna. This time, Krishna let Jarasandha get victory so that his ego is boosted up and will come for fight once again. Then Krishna fled to the ocean city of Dwaraka kingdom.
Bhattathiri worshipped Bhagwan to protect him from his ailments.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tadanu mathurāṃ gatvā hatvā camūṃ yavanāhṛtāṃ
magadhapatinā mārge sainyaiḥ pureva nivāritaḥ |
caramavijayaṃ darpāyāsmai pradāya palāyito
jaladhinagarīṃ yāto vātālayeśvara pāhi mām || 77-12 ||
